julia: Quick report from walking through the Go quickstart sample app: cancelling a generator stream while the token provider is doing a blocking refresh can hang the iterator.

pete: ouch. reproducible locally?

julia: yep. minimal snippet in sampleapp: 
```
for resp.Next() {
  if provider.NeedsRefresh() {
    provider.Refresh() // blocks on network call
  }
  handleChunk(resp.Event())
}
```
Canceling the ctx during Refresh() leaves Next() blocked and goroutines pile up.

token-bot: CI: flaky test stream-cancel-unit failed 2x on main, heap/goroutine spikes observed https://ci.internal/longjob/stream-cancel-failures

ken: We should make Refresh accept context (Refresh(ctx)) and have the SDK provide a helper TokenProviderWithContext that callers can use. Also ensure iterator.Close() explicitly closes the http response/body.

lisa: Agreed. Small fix: run Refresh in a separate goroutine and select on ctx.Done() so cancellation short-circuits refresh. But better to expose ctx in the API.

julia: I'll open issue with repro steps + trace. Leaning towards a tiny change: add TokenProviderWithContext in sdk/auth and update sampleapp to use it.

pete: Can we add a unit/integration test that starts a fake streaming server that stalls during auth, starts Generate(), then cancels after a couple tokens and asserts goroutine count doesn't grow?

ken: yes, fake server test sounds right. Keep it local/focused so CI stays fast.

lisa: Also add a Note in the streaming quickstart about non-blocking auth callbacks and a code example showing the context-aware pattern. JS/py already have similar examples.

julia: I'll draft a PR for the helper + sampleapp change + test and tag y'all for review. PR will reference issue #2104 in the repo.

token-bot: linked issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/2104 and CI job queued for next run.
